body.p: Applicant replies to the Office Action dated June 21, 2024, within two months. In the outstanding Office Action, the Examiner states that all pending claims in the application are subject to a restriction and requires Applicant to make an election.
According to the Office Action, the Examiner requires election of one of the following groups under 35 U.S.C. 121:
a. Group I - claims 1-10, drawn to a method of determining a repair method for a defect in a bladed rotor, including determining that a defect matches a known defect in a repair database;
b. Group II - claims 11-16, drawn to a method of determining a repair method for a defect in a bladed rotor including performing a structural simulation and an aerodynamic simulation; and

c. Group III - claims 17-20, drawn to a non-transitory computer readable storage medium for generating a repair process for a defect in response to a rotor module meeting aerodynamic performance criteria and structural criteria.

In reply, Applicant elects Group I, including claims 1-10 without traverse. This election is made without waiver, estoppel and without prejudice to the filing of one or more related applications directed to the unelected Group.

Applicant submits that the foregoing election conforms this application to the Examiner's requirement to elect a single disclosed invention. In light of the above amendments and remarks, Applicant respectfully submits all of the currently pending claims are in condition for examination on the merits. If the Examiner believes that a telephone conference would be useful in moving the application forward to allowance, the Examiner is encouraged to contact the undersigned. Applicant authorizes and respectfully requests that any fees due be charged to Deposit Account No. 19-2814. This statement does NOT authorize charge of the issue fee.
Gregg Scheiferstein, Reg. No. 77,204SNELL & WILMER L.L.P.
